messages:
marcus: Quick sync — ArcheTech reached out, they have a new NPU board and want a joint perf study (perf/W + throughput profiles + some kernel tuning). They can ship dev boards next week. Looking to schedule a 2-week benchmarking window. What should we scope?
anya: Important to decide instrumentation first. Need dmesg hooks, perf counters we care about (instructions, cache-misses, memory-bandwidth), and power telemetry sampling rate. Also driver patch access for kernel-level timers.
li: Agree. Also call out model execution paths we must validate: quantized INT8 path vs FP16 fallback. Need to exercise KV cache and large sequence performance for our runtime.
sofia: I'll draft the experiment matrix today: models (OPT-175M, Llama2-70B, decoding configs), batch sizes (1,4,8,16), seq lens (32,128,1024), power states (P0/P1), and thermal cabinet vs ambient. Acceptance criteria column too (latency < X ms at Y throughput, perf/W delta > Z).
kevin: Heads up — marketplace and comms: if this becomes a co-announce we need an embargo window and verified-badge checklist. Can we aim for a joint blog + marketplace performance badge if numbers pass?
sam_partner: From ArcheTech: we can provide 6 boards for test and a kernel engineer to help with driver hops. Prefer results embargoed until both sides sign off. We can also run a mirrored smoke run on our infra.
marcus: Good. Ownership proposal: Redwood runtime team (li + sofia) run primary bench and produce canonical results; ArcheTech runs mirrored smoke; partnerships (me/kevin) handle comms/embargo; eng-ml (sofia) owns metrics & thresholds. Agree?
anya: One caveat: kernel patches might change perf behavior. We should record git SHAs for any driver/firmware changes and re-run baseline if anything changes. Also capture thermal throttling events.
li: For tooling, prefer to use our bench harness. Example run command for smoke:
```
./bench-run --model llama2-70b --batch 4 --seq 128 --device archetech0 --trace perf,power --out s3://redwood-partner/archetech/smoke/
```
Make sure partner has s3 creds or we provide a presigned path.
sofia: I'll add telemetry tags: run_id, git_sha_runtime, kernel_sha, board_fw, ambient_temp. Also add unique sample ids for reproducibility.
bench-bot: Note: bench job created -> bench-1729876543-001, results destination s3://redwood-partner/archetech/bench-1729876543-001. Scheduler ETA: 2024-05-03 09:00 PT.
kevin: Timeline suggestion: week 1 = integration + smoke + kernel patch iteration; week 2 = full matrix + verification + writeup. Target joint blog draft by end of week 3.
sam_partner: Confirmed on our side. We'll ship boards Monday and provide kernel engineer contact (tara@archetech). Also can share power measurement harness doc: https://archetech.com/dev/power-harness (will send access).
marcus: Risks to call out: thermal headroom differences, early-silicon power calibration drift, and driver-induced determinism issues. We'll document mitigation (longer runs, retry logic, CI gating for kernel changes).
li: Measurement specifics: measure steady-state throughput after warmup window (e.g., ignore first 30s), report 50/90/99 latency, 95th-power and average power over window. Also provide CPU & host mem usage.
sofia: Action items: 1) I'll post experiment matrix & checklist by EOD. 2) Li will prepare bench harness config and presigned s3 path. 3) Anya will list perf counters and logging hooks. 4) Marcus/Keven will draft embargo + comms plan. Sam to confirm board ETA and kernel contact.
marcus: Sweet. If no objections I'll schedule a 30m kickoff with ArcheTech tomorrow 10:30 PT.
sam_partner: Works for us. Tara will join.
kevin: I'll book the meeting and invite marketplace.
marcus: Thanks all — keeping this thread for quick updates. Please ping me if you need priority access to labs or thermal chamber time. :thumbsup:
